decisions.reason: As a newly launched product that fits our reusable agriculture-packaging capabilities, its evidence is too limited after one year to judge it below aspiration, and a large firm like ours has enough slack to continue learning.
Its own product page signals meaningful early commitment and market relevance, so it meets at least a provisional aspiration level and should be retained while sales and customer feedback accumulate.

The stackable plastic crate is close to our core crate business, so even with only early website mention it is sensible to keep it on the market while we assess whether it can scale through existing customer channels.

Although early visibility is modest, the medium-duty rackable pallet is well aligned with our established pallet portfolio, and behavioral-theory logic suggests retaining it for another period rather than dropping it before results are clear.
The dedicated page suggests stronger initial positioning and the spill-retention pallet extends our pallet offering into a valuable compliance-oriented use case, so it should be kept.
The dedicated page and clear logistics-use benefit indicate a credible fit with customer needs and our engineering strengths, making retention the prudent choice at this early stage.
